institutionName: UiT The Arctic University of Norway

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I completed a master's thesis during my stay, and the following aspects were crucial:
- An (to me) academically relevant research group 
- A research community by which I broaden my professional network with
- The opportunities for outdoor activities

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The formalities and paperwork I had to complete before and during my stay dragged the experience down

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy but I did it all by myself

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not receive any in particular

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I did a master's project which apparently is kind of abnormal, so I just figured out everything either by myself or with help from my supervisor.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
It was easy to find housing - but finding a good place was difficult. I looked at
www.finn.no
,
www.hybel.no
and Facebook Marketplace.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
It can be rather expensive. Electricity can be expensive, so remember to add at least 500-600 NOK/month to the rent. 
Find housing either close to the university or city centre - or at least in a place close to a bus stop.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: As I did a master's thesis, there were some complications. Pretty sure it won't be a problem if one is taking regular courses.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You register your courses at "StudentWeb". Fairly straightforward.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The Mobility-unit at the university could help you per e-mail. They respond within a day or two.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you want to do a master's thesis, prepare well and contact both home and host university well in advance.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It generally seems a bit less ambitious compared to UCPH.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: As I did a master's project where I my own ambitions sat the level, I am not eligible to answer this. However, I got the feeling that the level in general is a bit lower as compared to UCPH.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I cannot answer this (as I did a master's project).

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 2 semesters

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
questions.answer: FSK3680 (special course code for master's thesis)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Only do a master's project abroad if you are prepared to do a lot of paperwork.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Food is generally expensive. Beers are inappropriately expensive. Cost of electricity can be expensive and fluctuate a lot.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Going out for drinks and food is very pricey.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Many opportunities. TSI (Tromsøstudentenes Idrettslag) has many options.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not sure about this

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Join one of the clubs of TSI. Buy a pair of backcountry skis (Toppturs-ski), take an avalanche course and go skiing from January-June.
Get a fishing rod and catch fish. They are everywhere.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go skiing, go to the mountains, go sailing. Just go outside

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Learn to talk Danish-Norwegian. Talk slowly and clearly and don't use slang words. That makes socialising with Norwegians easier.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: There were not any.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The Norwegians are very outdoorsy and are always ready to get outside.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Bring warm clothes no matter what time you get here
2. Bring a rain jacket
3. Get your hands on a car and go explore

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Without considering the academics, you should only go to Tromsø if you enjoy being outdoor. It is out of this world. Otherwise it can be a pretty harsh place. Dark, cold and wet.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The nature and outdoors has definitely been the best.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The constant urge to go into the mountains instead of the lab.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
